title: Which decimals can five digits make near thirty and above one hundred?
description: Using the digits 1, 4, 0, 8 and 6, we make the decimal closest to 30 and the smallest decimal between 100 and 1000, the same way as the example in the book.
teaching_notes: One idea: choose the digits before the point first, then put the smallest after it. Watch for children who start with a leading zero.

source: Figure it Out (end of chapter), Q5
video_script.why: The child has built a decimal near a target from given digits and now does it for two new targets.
video_script.substitution: Fix the digits before the point first, then put the smallest digits after the point.
video_script.anchor: The five digit tiles 1, 4, 0, 8 and 6 with two targets: closest to 30, and smallest between 100 and 1000.
video_script.payoff_line: Choose the digits before the point first, and keep the smallest for after it

final_answer.spoken: forty point one six eight, and one hundred and four point six eight

maths_rules: (a) no digit 3; tens digit 4 is 1 away from 3, tens digit 1 is 2 away
tens 4, smallest digits after the point: 40.168, gap 40.168 - 30 = 10.168
(b) between 100 and 1000 means three digits before the point: smallest non-zero 1, then 0, then 4, then 6 and 8 in order: 104.68
check: 100 < 104.68 < 1000, and the next smallest 104.86 is larger
video_script.design: The five digit tiles stay on the board with a movable point. Each try is built under them and its gap to 30 is bracketed.

beats.on_screen: Given: digits 1, 4, 0, 8, 6, each used once; target 30; range 100 to 1000
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the digits one, four, zero, eight and six, each used once.

beats.on_screen: To find: (a) the decimal closest to 30 (b) the smallest decimal between 100 and 1000
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find two decimals.
<bookmark mark='fa'/>One is closest to thirty.
<bookmark mark='fb'/>The other is the smallest between one hundred and one thousand.

beats.on_screen: (a) no digit 3; tens digit 4 is 1 away from 3; tens digit 1 is 2 away from 3

marks.a1: the tile three is crossed out
marks.a2: the tiles four and one move to the tens place in turn

narration: <bookmark mark='a1'/>Step one, there is no digit three to use.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>The tens digit four is one away from three. The tens digit one is two away.

beats.on_screen: tens 4, smallest digits after the point: 40.168; 40.168 - 30 = 10.168

marks.t1: the tiles line up as forty point one six eight
marks.t2: the gap is bracketed on the line

narration: <bookmark mark='t1'/>Step two, try four tens, with the smallest digits after the point.
<bookmark mark='t2'/>That gives forty point one six eight. It is ten point one six eight above thirty.

marks.o1: the tiles line up as eighteen point six four zero

narration: <bookmark mark='o1'/>Step three, try one ten, with the greatest number below twenty. That is eighteen point six four zero.
<bookmark mark='o2'/>Thirty minus that is eleven point three six. Ten point one six eight is smaller, so forty point one six eight is closer.

beats.on_screen: (b) between 100 and 1000: three digits before the point; 1, then 0, then 4, then 6 and 8: 104.68

marks.b1: three places before the point are marked
marks.b2: the tiles one, zero and four fill them
marks.b3: the tiles six and eight fill the places after the point

narration: <bookmark mark='b1'/>Step four, a number between one hundred and one thousand has three digits before the point.
<bookmark mark='b2'/>Start with the smallest digit that is not zero, which is one. Then zero, then four.
<bookmark mark='b3'/>Six and eight follow in order, after the point. That gives one hundred and four point six eight.

beats.on_screen: check: 100 < 104.68 < 1000; the next smallest, 104.86, is larger

marks.chk: a tick appears beside the range
marks.nxt: the swap of six and eight is shown

narration: <bookmark mark='chk'/>Step five, check. One hundred and four point six eight is more than one hundred and less than one thousand.
<bookmark mark='nxt'/>The next smallest, one hundred and four point eight six, is larger.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Choose the digits before the point first, and keep the smallest for after it.
<bookmark mark='va'/>The closest to thirty is forty point one six eight.
<bookmark mark='vb'/>The smallest between one hundred and one thousand is one hundred and four point six eight.
